headline: Palantir's chief technology officer has said, without evidence, that some AI researchers have started smoking to show how much they believe in AI, and called the mood in Silicon Valley a "mass psychosis".
score_reason: Pool score kept at the watchlist level: a colourful quote with no evidence behind its main claim.
importance_line: A senior executive at a firm that sells to governments dismissing AI-safety fears as groupthink shapes how the public hears the safety debate, then the rules that follow, then AI firms, but he gives no evidence for the smoking claim or for his share of researchers, and Fortune says it is unclear how many researchers actually smoke.
summary: Fortune reports that Shyam Sankar, chief technology officer of Palantir, a US software company that analyses data for governments and businesses, told CBS's "Face the Nation" that "so many researchers have started smoking as a way of signaling to other researchers how much they believe in AI", citing no evidence, and called the mood in Silicon Valley around AI a "mass psychosis" and "social delusion". Fortune adds that he repeated, again without evidence, that "the vast majority" of US AI researchers follow effective altruism (a movement that tries to do the most good by reasoned argument), which he called a "millenarian doomsday cult", and that Palantir has stocked free nicotine pouches in its Washington, D.C., office.
notes: Read from fulltext. The date of the CBS interview is not stated.
